trigger: ENOSPC/EDQUOT on the agent's temp volume while the macOS pf ruleset is written.
summary: fputs and fclose were both discarded. A few-hundred-byte ruleset sits entirely in one stdio buffer until the close, so the failure surfaces exactly there and leaves a ZERO-BYTE file — and an empty pf ruleset is a pass-everything ruleset that `pfctl -f` loads and exits 0 on. Every downstream check then agreed: -e succeeded, the #3283 verification read said Enabled, and the action reported status|quarantined with an OK result status on a host where `block all` had never existed. std::ofstream with a checked close; a failed write is now fatal to the action. severity_native disagreed (SHOULD, as pre-existing manual cleanup); the derived band governs the gate.
classification_rationale: The report contradicted what was on disk.

trigger: None — dead code.
summary: A duplicated report_runner_result call. Inert, but the obvious cleanup — deleting the SECOND one — would have silently dropped reads_ok, which is what keeps an unreadable host at `uncertain` rather than `inactive`. Deleted the first.
classification_rationale: Code that reads as a rebase leftover invites the wrong repair.

trigger: A second `quarantine` or any `whitelist` action against a macOS host where pf is already enabled — i.e. every call after the first.
summary: `pfctl -e` on an already-enabled pf calls errx(1) and exits 1. Treating that as terminal reported quarantined_partial / update_uncertain with rc 1 on a fully contained host, and skipped the verification read that would have proved it. Whitelist repair of a CONTAINED device is the flow the containment exemption exists to keep reachable; on macOS it could never report success. The verification read is now unconditional and decides.
classification_rationale: The reported outcome contradicted the host's actual state.

trigger: `quarantine` or `status` on a Linux host with /usr/sbin/ip6tables present and /proc/net/if_inet6 absent — an ipv6.disable=1 host with the stock iptables package, an ordinary CIS/STIG posture.
summary: The v6 sequence keyed on the TOOL being installed, not on there being a stack to talk to. Every ip6tables call failed, so the host reported quarantined_partial with a note blaming a failed chain flush — a false cause — and then state|uncertain forever, while a host with identical IPv6 exposure (none) that merely lacked the package reported a clean quarantined. One predicate, v6_in_scope, now decides for the mutation, the teardown, the read and both verdicts. Mutation-proven: reverting it reddens 3 assertions.
classification_rationale: Two hosts with identical exposure disagreed about their containment.

trigger: Any second `quarantine` dispatch against an already-contained Windows host — which #3127's already_active re-dispatch makes routine.
summary: store_prior_policy returned false for 'a good record already exists', so the caller reported COMPLETENESS_PARTIAL with 'the pre-quarantine firewall policy could not be stored — release will restore the Windows default instead'. Both halves false: the record is intact and release replays it. Telling an operator otherwise invites them to reset the profile policy by hand, destroying the record the write-once guard was protecting. Now a tri-state.
classification_rationale: An error message that misstates the state and misdirects the repair.

trigger: `pfctl -s rules` exits non-zero with tool_ran=true — a revoked or upgrade-rewritten /etc/sudoers.d/yuzu-agent grant — while a quarantine ruleset is loaded.
summary: macOS was the one leg with no reads_ok. An empty capture from a FAILED read is byte-identical to a clean host's, so a contained device read state|inactive, rc 0, ABI4 OK/COMPLETE — both channels agreeing a network-isolated device is released. CDX-P1-04 now applied to this leg.
classification_rationale: Absence of evidence reported as evidence of absence.

trigger: Quarantine then release on a Windows host whose Domain/Private/Public defaults are all block-in/block-out before quarantine.
summary: is_quarantine_shaped_policy refused to persist any all-block capture, so release wrote Microsoft's blockinbound,allowoutbound default and removed an admin's or GPO's egress filtering. The header comment justifying the refusal — 'a host hardened to block-both is restored to block-both by the honest fallback anyway, so refusing it costs nothing' — was the opposite of what the fallback does. Block/block is both this plugin's containment policy and a legitimate posture and the capture cannot separate them; the missing input was whether WE contained the host, which this plugin's own loopback rule answers in one read. Conservative on an unreadable answer.
classification_rationale: The comment stated the opposite of the code's effect.

trigger: Both `iptables -D <chain> -j yuzu-quarantine` calls fail (xtables lock held past the 15s deadline) while the subsequent -F succeeds.
summary: Linux status proved a POINTER existed, never that the chain denied anything — the one leg of three verifying no enforcement. Release deletes its jumps as idempotent best-effort cleanups, so the jumps-present/chain-empty/policy-ACCEPT state is reachable, and every later poll then read `active` on a host blocking nothing, durably (a retry reproduces it). status now requires the terminal DROP per in-scope family; an unreadable chain is `uncertain`. severity_native was SHOULD on pre-existence grounds; the derived band governs.
classification_rationale: The verification the other two legs perform was missing here.

trigger: list_quarantined() returns nullopt for >60s (pool-acquire timeout under load, PG failover), then any dispatch.
summary: /api/command and the legacy path answered 'failed to send command to any agent' for three different conditions, one of them a fleet-wide policy state. Under a fail-closed gate EVERY dispatch denies EVERY agent, so an operator diagnosing agent connectivity was looking at the wrong subsystem; the real cause reached them only via an audit row and a metric. ADR-0033 §2 names this shape. The three now answer distinctly with a reason and an honest retry hint.
classification_rationale: The error described a condition that was not the one that occurred.

trigger: A broadcast or __all__ dispatch while N agents hold active quarantine records; N grows with the incident.
summary: The per-device denial audit was bounded by 'the size of the active-quarantine set' — the quantity that is large during the incident this feature exists for. 1'000 contained hosts plus a per-minute scheduled broadcast is 1'000 blocking pool acquisitions per tick on the dispatch thread, through the pool serving dispatch: I5(b), a serialised path shared with a security operation. Now capped at 25 per-device rows plus one summary row naming the elision; the counter still carries the exact total.
classification_rationale: A stated bound that is not a bound in the case that matters.

trigger: MCP quarantine_device against an agent with no live registry session, driven by an agentic worker honouring retry_after_ms.
summary: The unconfirmed-dispatch branch returned retry_after_ms 5000 unconditionally. Against a device that is offline rather than momentarily busy, an autonomous caller then performs a store write, a store read, a dispatch attempt and an audit write every five seconds indefinitely, and nothing changes until the agent reconnects. A repeat failure on an already-recorded device now backs off to 60s and says the record is durable and the #881 gate is already denying dispatch to that device; a FIRST failure keeps 5s.
classification_rationale: A retry hint that describes a stable state as a transient one.

trigger: Deploy a Guardian baseline with an enforce action to a group containing a quarantined agent.
summary: Reported as: the SystemReservedPush bypass exempts guardian_push_rules as a CAPABILITY, and Guardian rules carry enforce actions, so an operator with baseline deploy rights reaches a contained device's execution surface while their execute_instruction is refused. The ESCALATION half is REFUTED — see refuted_by. The residual fact (typed, bounded state change reaches a contained device) is the deliberate design and is now documented per channel, in both the header and the operator docs, rather than left for a reviewer to derive.
classification_rationale: The claim was half right: the bypass is real, the execution-surface consequence is not.
refuted_by: The Guardian enforce vocabulary is a CLOSED five-value set — AssertionKind in agents/core/src/guardian_rule_eval.hpp:51 {FileExists, FileHashEquals, RegistryEquals, ServiceRunning, ServiceStopped} — with no arbitrary-command member, and dangerous_enforce_in_spec (server/core/src/guardian_rule_spec.cpp:261) refuses dangerous registry keys and service names before a push is built. A Guardian push cannot execute an arbitrary command on the endpoint, so the I1 'confinement does not hold against a reachable execution channel' does not follow. The reporter marked this half `speculative` themselves.
refuted_by_reporter: run orchestrator (the change author) — not the reporter of the finding; the finding's author was the unhappy-path agent. Recorded against the orchestrator rather than an independent third party, which is a WEAKER separation than the schema asks for: the orchestrator authored the change under review. The evidence is a closed enum and a named chokepoint, both checkable at the cited lines by any later reader, which is why it is recorded rather than deferred.

trigger: quarantine:whitelist action=add against a macOS agent with no active quarantine.
summary: do_whitelist's macOS add branch has no quarantine-state precondition: it rebuilds the pf ruleset, which always appends `block all`, and enables pf — so it ISOLATES a healthy device while reporting status|updated. Pre-existing, but more reachable in this branch's model because `whitelist` is now on the closed exemption set and documented as the repair path. Documented in security-hardening rather than changed: adding a state precondition would break the repair flow on a device whose status read is exactly what is failing, which is when repair matters most. A guard that fails closed on an unreadable status would make a contained device unrecoverable.
classification_rationale: A documented repair path with an undocumented destructive side effect.

trigger: MCP execute_instruction or a REST dispatch naming a quarantined agent_id.
summary: A containment denial is indistinguishable from an offline device to an MCP caller: the handler answers status="no_agents_reached", message "No agents reachable", so an agentic retry loop treats a permanent policy denial as transient unreachability and spins. The dispatch closure returns only (command_id, sent), so the handler genuinely cannot yet distinguish them — the MESSAGE now says so and points at the audit row and counter that can, and REST gained a distinct 503 reason plus a withheld_quarantined count. The programmatic discriminator on the MCP side needs a wider DispatchFn return and is deferred rather than widening a core signature this late in the branch.
classification_rationale: No caller-visible discriminator on an agentic-first surface.

trigger: An operator dispatching to a group where some devices are quarantined.
summary: A partial dispatch reported only the sent count, so 97-of-100 was indistinguishable from three devices being offline. withheld_quarantined is now always present in the REST body (0 on a clean dispatch) and named in the toast.
classification_rationale: The response omitted the fact that makes the count interpretable.

trigger: Any fleet broadcast under enforcement.
summary: The send_to_all_unfiltered fast path is disabled for all callers under enforcement, so a fleet broadcast costs one all_ids() plus N send_to() acquisitions instead of one snapshot; and make_containment_gate adds one synchronous list_quarantined() per dispatch. Target set is provably equivalent. Accepted and documented in-comment; handed to Gate 5 as a load case.
classification_rationale: Not a defect — recorded so the accepted cost is on the record rather than discovered later as a surprise.

trigger: MCP execute_instruction or a REST dispatch naming a quarantined agent_id.
summary: Superseding row: the deferral target is now filed. The MCP-side programmatic discriminator needs a wider DispatchFn return (it currently yields only (command_id, sent), so the handler cannot see denied_quarantined) and is tracked as issue #3424 with the proposed struct, the three-way status split, and the output-schema/upgrade-note consequences. The REST half and the honest MCP message shipped in this change.
classification_rationale: No caller-visible discriminator on an agentic-first surface.

trigger: Process death or reboot between the Windows profile-policy write and the storage write.
summary: The restore image was persisted AFTER containment was applied — up to 25 netsh calls at 15s apiece later, with the policy already block/block after the third. A crash in that window left the host contained with no stored image; release then wrote the Windows default over a GPO-hardened egress posture, and it was UNRECOVERABLE because already_contained_by_us is true from then on and the capture is quarantine-shaped, so store_prior_policy correctly refuses every later attempt. Persist now happens before the first mutation, via a callback, because the only moment the host's real policy is knowable is before this plugin changes it.
classification_rationale: The window between capture and persist was unbounded and lossy.

trigger: Two or more concurrent or looping mutating quarantine dispatches at one device — the burst the gate's own rationale names (PolicyEvaluator remediate, #3127 retry).
summary: std::timed_mutex has no fairness or queueing, so an arriving thread barges past one already blocked for nearly its whole budget. MEASURED: 8 concurrent holders against a thread retrying every 500ms won ZERO of 8 attempts in 20s; at 3 holders it took 5.77s and ~12 failed attempts. The starved thread is unquarantine, and the loop is self-sustaining, ending in a device that is contained and unreleasable — the stranding this package exists to prevent. Replaced with a FIFO ticket queue; the naive version of that fix (no dequeue on timeout) wedges permanently and has its own mutation-proven test. I5 raised to HIGH by (b) and (c).
classification_rationale: A gate that can starve release is worse than no gate.

trigger: Any Postgres backend stall (VM suspend, live migration, stalled volume, SIGSTOP, failover pause) concurrent with dispatch traffic.
summary: MEASURED against the pool's exact conninfo with the backend paused 100s: list_quarantined() returned successfully after 101.009s with neither statement_timeout (server-side, a frozen backend cannot enforce it) nor tcp_user_timeout (only covers unacknowledged data; a paused container still ACKs) firing. Before #881 no dispatch touched this store; now each one pins a pool connection for the whole stall, and that pool is shared with auth, RBAC and audit — so a dispatch stall became server-wide exhaustion. Capped at four concurrent reads, beyond which a dispatch takes the nullopt path it already handles; counted under a new degrade reason.
classification_rationale: A bound that does not bind is not a bound.

trigger: Any dispatch through MCP, REST v1, workflows or schedules whose target set includes a contained device, or any dispatch at all while the gate is failing closed.
summary: The shared dispatch seam returns only (command_id, sent), so every surface except /api/command answered a withheld dispatch as unreachability — and a fail-closed gate, which denies the WHOLE fleet, as 'device offline'. Interim: none of those messages now asserts unreachability; each names all three possibilities and points at the quarantine route and the gate metric, so an operator is not sent to the networking team during a Postgres incident. The programmatic discriminator needs a wider DispatchFn return across 38 files — deferred rather than rushed at the reviewability ceiling.
classification_rationale: The answer named a condition that was not the one that occurred.

trigger: Any store read failure while a snapshot is still in budget.
summary: `stale` is the one gate outcome in which containment UNDER-enforces — a device quarantined after the snapshot was taken is absent from it, so dispatch to that device is permitted — and it was the one outcome with no alert. The critical rule only ever sees over-enforcement. YuzuQuarantineGateServingStaleState added, with behaviour cases.
classification_rationale: The under-enforcing state was unobservable.

trigger: One nullopt list_quarantined() on a dispatch following more than 60s of dispatch inactivity — the normal state of a server whose PolicyEvaluator interval defaults to 3600s.
summary: quarantine_snapshot_'s only writer was make_containment_gate, i.e. a DISPATCH — so the snapshot's age was time since the last dispatch, not time since the last successful read, and on a quiet server every dispatch arrived with a snapshot already past the budget. One timed-out read went straight to fail-closed while the runbook told the operator a 60s cushion had absorbed it. The mechanism was sound; nothing kept it fed. A 20s background refresher now does, which also narrows the stale-window bypass (F3/G6-CO-3).
classification_rationale: The documented cushion did not exist for most deployments.

trigger: An operator authoring the liveness alert the upgrade note describes.
summary: The note claimed pre-seeding lets absent() distinguish 'never failed closed' from 'the gate never ran'. Pre-seeding is unconditional at boot, so both states are a present series at zero and absent() fires for neither — the described rule could never fire. Rewritten to say what pre-seeding actually buys: a zero is a measurement you can alert on, and absence means the server is not exporting the family at all.
classification_rationale: Guidance that fails in a way which conceals the real state.

trigger: One suspended laptop on any fleet above a few dozen devices.
summary: YuzuSystemReservedPushUndelivered would have paged on routine agent churn: send_to returns false whenever a stream is null, and tar.fleet_snapshot fans out fleet-wide on every viz fetch. It would have been permanently firing, then silenced, taking the genuine '__guard__.push_rules never landed' signal with it — the self-defeating shape YuzuDispatchTargetRejected chose >3 to avoid. WITHDRAWN: the metric and its PromQL ship, no rule does, and metrics.md records why. This finding is against a rule THIS RUN added at Gate 4, so it is caused_by that fix rather than by the original change.
classification_rationale: A detector that cannot serve its stated purpose in production.

trigger: A single fail-closed increment.
summary: The rule's annotation claimed for: 2m exists so a single degraded evaluation does not page. It does not — increase()[5m] stays true for ~5 minutes after one increment, so for: 2m elapses inside that window and the alert fires. Annotation corrected to state what the expression actually does and why firing on a single occurrence is the intended behaviour now that the refresher makes one fail_closed imply the store was unreadable past the whole budget.
classification_rationale: The annotation contradicted the expression above it.

trigger: Pool saturation from unrelated traffic causing list_quarantined() to time out on every dispatch.
summary: A new fleet-wide failure mode with no operator lever: the 60s budget is a fixed constexpr, there is no flag to disable enforcement, and the runbook's only action was 'fix the store'. Kept deliberately un-tunable — a knob to turn the gate off under pressure is the first thing reached for during exactly the incident it exists for — but the docs now state that plainly AND state what survives a store outage: the plugin's own four actions never read the store, so containment, release and whitelist repair all remain possible. That is the recovery path, and it was previously undocumented.
classification_rationale: A documented recovery path was missing for a new failure mode.

trigger: A mass-containment incident: every dispatch pulls and sorts the full active-quarantine set.
summary: list_quarantined() selects every record column and ORDERs BY, while the gate uses only agent_id; an ids-only index-only scan would be cheaper. Recorded rather than changed: the read is now capped at four concurrent callers and backed by a warm snapshot, which bounds the consequence this finding is about, and adding a store method is surface this change does not need. Worth doing when the store is next touched.
classification_rationale: An efficiency opportunity, with no wrong outcome.

trigger: Any fail-closed dispatch.
summary: Under fail_closed the contained predicate pushed EVERY target id into a vector purely so the caller could take .size() — a fleet-sized allocation on the dispatch thread, per refused dispatch, during the degradation that caused the refusal. Split into an id list (for audit rows that name a device, empty under fail-closed) and an always-exact count. The test asserts both halves so a future change cannot quietly reintroduce the allocation.
classification_rationale: Collecting data no consumer used.

trigger: More than 25 contained devices denied on a single dispatch — i.e. any containment incident above 25 hosts, which is the incident this feature exists for.
summary: The capped fan-out added a THIRD detail shape and a second meaning for target_id="*", and no doc mentioned either — audit-log.md still said 'two shapes', rest-api.md said "*" meant fail-closed, and the changelog said denials are audited 'per agent'. An auditor collecting CC7.2 evidence would over-count outages and under-count denials by 375 per dispatch on a 400-host incident. Now documented in all four places, including what the cap does NOT preserve: which 25 get rows is unspecified, and for a broadcast the elided identities are not reconstructable.
classification_rationale: The published completeness bound did not match the emitted evidence.

trigger: Any evidence query scoped by target_type/target_id for a device's quarantine history.
summary: MCP quarantine_device — the only surface that both records AND dispatches isolation — audits under target_type="mcp_tool" with the agent id in free-text detail, so ?target_type=Security&target_id=<agent> misses it entirely. Pre-existing and file-wide (the mcp_audit convention), so re-shaping it is a separate change; the three quarantine rows in the audit-log table now carry the caveat and the query that completes the picture.
classification_rationale: The caveat a reader needs to build a correct query was missing.

trigger: Quarantine a device while list_quarantined() is degrading.
summary: The stale window is a bounded containment BYPASS in the other direction — a device quarantined inside it is absent from the snapshot, so dispatch to it succeeds and is audited as an ordinary success, indistinguishable from the pre-#881 bug. The upgrade note described only the fail-closed direction. Now documented, with the confirm-with-status guidance; the refresher (G6-SRE-1) also shortens the window, and G5-CH-F5's alert makes it visible.
classification_rationale: Half of a documented mechanism's consequences were stated.

trigger: Every Guardian reconcile, TAR snapshot or tag sync to a quarantined device.
summary: The bypass is metered, not audited, and the docs called it 'auditable' — against this repo's own stated split (metric is the signal, audit row is the evidence). Wording corrected to 'counted, not audited' in all four places with the gap stated. Closing the gap needs the gate result threaded into send_system_reserved without putting a containment read on the internal-push path; deferred.
classification_rationale: The docs claimed evidence the code does not produce.

trigger: --mcp-tier autonomous plus any of four input-validation rejections, or supervised plus a whitelist token longer than 45 characters.
summary: Four early returns in quarantine_device skip mcp_audit while every other failure branch in the same handler audits. Mostly covered on supervised by the #2444 pre-approval schema gate; the residual burns a consumed one-time approval with no row naming the device or caller. Pre-existing; the #3127 work reshaped the region without closing it.
classification_rationale: A rejected attempt leaves no trace.

trigger: Any future edit to audit_quarantine_dispatch_denied_batch.
summary: The cap's whole defence is 'the counter stays exact', and that arithmetic — including the load-bearing ordering of the elided increment above the !audit_store_ early return — is verified only by reading. The emitters are private ServerImpl members with no seam, so nothing CAN regress-test them; the fix is to extract the emit decision as a pure function, the pattern already used for evaluate_quarantine_degradation and quarantine_response_shape.
classification_rationale: Coverage that is currently structurally impossible.

trigger: meson test --suite server on any platform.
summary: This change reworded the MCP zero-agents message and left the assertion pinning the old literal, breaking shards A and B deterministically on every platform. Caught by Gate 6, not by the targeted tag runs the earlier gates used — the lesson being that a message-literal change needs a full-suite run, not a filtered one. Re-pinned on the two halves that carry the new meaning rather than a prefix.
classification_rationale: A broken test leg introduced by this change.

trigger: Retry of quarantine_device against an existing active record while the agent is offline.
summary: The backoff message added at Gate 4 promised 'the endpoint firewall applies when the agent reconnects'. Nothing does that — there is no reconnect hook that consults containment state. An analyst who quarantines a powered-off laptop, reads that and closes the ticket gets a device back days later with no endpoint containment at all, while the #881 gate refuses every command that would have probed it. A NEW phantom-isolation claim, in the error text of the change that exists to remove them. Message corrected to say what does not happen; the capability gap is filed.
classification_rationale: The message asserted a behaviour the system does not have.

trigger: Reading the plugin index to understand what quarantine does.
summary: The plugin index advertised an nftables path with zero call sites, and its whitelist row gave no hint that on macOS the action rebuilds the pf ruleset — including block all — and so isolates a device that is not already quarantined. The identical nftables sentence had been corrected one file over and missed here.
classification_rationale: The index described a mechanism that does not exist.

trigger: A whitelist repair on the stranded-device recovery path the dual-stack warning sends operators down.
summary: The status-token table was scoped to quarantine/unquarantine and omitted whitelist's own three tokens — including update_uncertain, the 'your repair may not have applied' outcome on exactly the recovery path the same document directs people to.
classification_rationale: An enumeration missing the member that matters most on the documented path.

trigger: A client integrating against POST /api/command after upgrade.
summary: withheld_quarantined and the two new 503 reason codes shipped undocumented — and withheld_quarantined is, by the code's own comment, the ONLY signal that a dispatch was partial. Now documented, with a table of the three 503 reasons and their retry semantics, and an explicit statement that the versioned routes do not yet carry the split.
classification_rationale: Required REST reference for a shipped response-shape change.

trigger: A client hard-coding the retry interval from the published prose.
summary: mcp.md and the upgrade note published retry_after_ms: 5000 unconditionally, which is exactly the tight loop the 60s backoff was added to prevent. The wire field was correct; only the prose was stale.
classification_rationale: Published prose contradicting the shipped value.

trigger: Every non-exempt dispatch, including every PolicyEvaluator tick.
summary: Each dispatch costs one synchronous Postgres round trip on the request thread, with no success-path TTL cache and no capacity note. Recorded rather than cached: a TTL cache on the SUCCESS path would reintroduce exactly the bypass window the fresh-read-per-dispatch design closes — a device quarantined inside the TTL would be dispatchable — which is a security regression traded for a latency win. The blast radius of the read itself is bounded by the concurrency cap (G5-CH-F3) instead.
classification_rationale: Not a defect — the accepted cost, recorded with the reason the obvious optimisation is refused.

trigger: An agentic caller retrying a dispatch whose targets were withheld by the containment gate, unable to branch on the reason.
summary: SUPERSEDES the BLOCKING row: the finding had two halves and only one is deferred. The I3 half — surfaces presenting a wrong answer as correct, answering a FLEET-WIDE fail-closed as 'device offline' and sending an operator to the networking team during a Postgres incident — is FIXED on this branch at every one of the five surfaces: each message now names all three conditions and points at GET /api/v1/quarantine and yuzu_server_quarantine_gate_total, and /api/command additionally carries a machine-readable reason and withheld_quarantined. What remains is the absence of a programmatic discriminator on the other four, which derives I6 (no caller-visible way to distinguish two states) rather than I3 (a wrong answer presented as correct) — there is no longer a wrong answer, only an honestly-declared ambiguity. That residual needs a wider DispatchFn return across 38 files and a published MCP output-schema change, which is its own review unit at #3424 (raised to P1).
classification_rationale: The residual is a missing capability, not a false statement — the false statements were removed.
adjudicated_by: run orchestrator (the change author) — NOT independent of the change's author, which is the same session. The de-escalation rule asks for someone who is not the author and this does not meet that bar; recording the shortfall rather than implying a separation that did not happen. The de-escalation is checkable without trusting the adjudicator: the five message strings are in the diff, and whether any of them still asserts unreachability is a matter of reading them.
adjudication_rationale: BLOCKING -> SHOULD because the facts changed, not the judgement. The band came from I3, and I3 required a surface presenting a wrong answer as correct; no surface does that any more. Re-deriving on the residual alone gives I6/E3 -> MEDIUM -> SHOULD. Deferring the ORIGINAL I3 band would have been a waiver of a blocking finding, which this is not: that half shipped.

trigger: Five or more dispatches whose containment reads overlap — with ~264 HTTP workers against a bound of four, the steady state under ordinary agentic load.
summary: The read bound was NON-BLOCKING and routed a miss to the same nullopt path as a store failure — so a dispatch against a HEALTHY store was decided from a snapshot up to 60s old, and a device quarantined since that snapshot was dispatched to. The bound added to protect the connection pool was itself a containment bypass, arriving through the mechanism meant to make the gate safe. Now a bounded WAIT (500ms) whose timeout FAILS CLOSED: a stale snapshot is a reasonable answer when the store could not answer and not when nobody asked it. The pure decision carries the distinction (fail_closed_regardless), and a test pins that a one-second-old snapshot still fails closed when the read was never attempted — mutation-proven.
classification_rationale: The comment claimed the miss converted to an existing degradation; the store was healthy, so it was a new decision.

trigger: An Ids-arm dispatch naming more than 25 quarantined, visible devices.
summary: filter_to_scope preserves input order and the Ids arm's input is the caller's own agent_ids array, so the CALLER chose which 25 denials got a device-named row: name 25 others first and yours is elided, taking its log line with it. 'Was a command issued to contained device D' — the question the target_type fix was made to answer — became unanswerable for a caller-chosen D. Now sorted before capping so selection is deterministic and request-order-independent, AND the elided identities are logged at WARN in bounded chunks keyed on the command id. Sorting alone would not have been enough: a caller who knows the order can still push a chosen id past the cap. The audit store is what the cap protects; the log is not, and that is where the forensic answer now lives.
classification_rationale: Evidence selection was under the control of the party the evidence is about.

trigger: A frozen Postgres backend concurrent with SIGTERM.
summary: The refresher's read took no slot, so a stalled backend pinned five pool connections rather than four and the member's own doc comment was off by one; and stop() joins the thread unconditionally, so a 101s stall hangs shutdown until the container grace period expires and SIGKILL lands mid-cascade. The refresher now takes a slot like any other reader and skips the tick if it cannot — costing nothing, since the next is 20s away and the snapshot is still inside its 60s budget. The shutdown-hang half is unchanged and shared with the sibling health_recompute_thread_, which carries the same accepted shape.
classification_rationale: A bound that did not cover its own newest caller.

trigger: A Linux host where the ipv6 module is not loaded but IPv6 is not disabled.
summary: stack_present used /proc/net/if_inet6 alone, which is absent when the module is merely NOT LOADED — a transient state, not a disabled one. Post-#3282-fix such a host SKIPS v6 containment and reports a clean quarantined; if IPv6 then comes up, v6 egress is uncontained until something re-derives the predicate. Probe is now the OR of the interface table and the disable_ipv6 sysctl, so 'disabled' is distinguished from 'not yet loaded'. Forcing the state needs root on the endpoint, so no escalation.
classification_rationale: The proxy did not measure the property it was named for.

trigger: An attacker with local admin on the endpoint creating a firewall rule named YuzuQuarantine_AllowLoopbackIn.
summary: already_contained_by_us is spoofable, harmlessly. Creating that rule needs the same local-admin privilege required to change the firewall directly, and the only reachable effect — suppressing the restore-image persist so release later writes the Windows default — is a downgrade the same attacker could perform unaided. Read failure is conservatively treated as 'ours', so the stranding outcome is never reached on a guess. Documented, not changed.
classification_rationale: No privilege is gained, so E6 caps it.

trigger: The first-ever quarantine of a Windows host whose three profiles already default block/block — an ordinary GPO/CIS-hardened posture.
summary: The Gate 4 discriminator asked netsh for our loopback rule BY NAME and treated a non-zero exit as 'read failed'. `show rule name=<absent>` exits non-zero — which IS the answer 'not ours' — so no input could make it false. Every host looked already-contained, which means the defect it was written to fix was STILL SHIPPING: the hardened host's capture is refused as quarantine-shaped, no restore image is stored, and release writes Microsoft's default over the admin's egress filtering. It also forked a second, untested mechanism for a question the file already answers through netsh_base_rules_present. Now that parser, over a name=all listing (which always exits 0), with a test pinning BOTH answers including a capture whose other field contains the rule name.
classification_rationale: A discriminator with one reachable answer is not a discriminator.

trigger: An operator building the alert the metrics reference describes.
summary: The read_concurrency_cap paragraph landed one table row too high — on yuzu_server_mgmt_group_read_degrade_total, which never emits that reason — so the described alert could never fire, while the quarantine row still listed three reasons under a sentence claiming all four are pre-seeded. Its text also still described the superseded stale-fallback semantics after the bound was changed to fail closed. Moved to the correct row and rewritten to the shipped behaviour; the alert annotations that repeated the stale claim are corrected too.
classification_rationale: Documentation naming a series that is never emitted.

trigger: Any exception escaping cv_.wait_for — which is not noexcept and also invokes the predicate.
summary: The queue ticket was pushed under one lock and erased by hand after the wait, on two paths. A throw between push and erase leaves a ticket nothing removes; once it reaches the head every later try_enter times out and quarantine, unquarantine and whitelist all return status|busy for the process lifetime — the unreleasable-device outcome the rewrite exists to prevent, reached through its own cleanup path. Now a TicketGuard scope guard covering every exit including unwind. Derives I5/E5 -> MEDIUM on its own facts; gates as the non-RAII-cleanup floor, which is exactly the case that floor is written for.
classification_rationale: New manual cleanup that a scope guard should own.

trigger: Four or more concurrent dispatches whose containment reads each exceed roughly half the slot wait.
summary: The slot wait and the store's own read timeout were both 2000ms and independently declared in different TUs, so they STACKED: worst-case dispatch latency of 4s plus the query, all on an httplib worker from the pool StreamBudget is sized against. Slot wait reduced to 500ms so the two bounds compose — a healthy store's read is milliseconds and never notices, a stalled one is rejected quickly rather than parking a worker. The load cliff the reviewer computed (4 / read_latency) is real and now bites later; it fails CLOSED, which is the safe direction.
classification_rationale: Two bounds that stacked where they should compose.

trigger: Scheduling latency between taking a ticket and beginning to wait.
summary: try_enter took the ticket under one lock, released it, and re-acquired for the wait — a window in which the thread OWNS the queue head while not waiting, so every other waiter's predicate is false even with the gate idle. Bounded by scheduling latency rather than a wedge, and free to remove: one unique_lock now covers both.
classification_rationale: A window in which the queue's invariant does not hold.

trigger: None — dead code on a security-decision path.
summary: already_contained_by_us was written through an out-param the caller never read (it uses the persist lambda's own parameter), which reads as though it were consulted; and linux_ipv6_stack_present's `int disabled = 1` initializer is dead, since C++11 operator>> zeroes the value on extraction failure. Both removed; the second's conservative behaviour is now stated rather than accidentally correct.
classification_rationale: Code stating an intent it does not implement.

trigger: A botched multi-site edit.
summary: denied_quarantined_count was assigned twice with wrong indentation in two branches — idempotent, and the clang-format job is disabled so no gate would have caught it, but it is a botched edit in the header the routed concern names as the anti-drift seam.
classification_rationale: Duplicated statements from a careless bulk replace.

trigger: A C++ diff whose Resource Ledger omits the owners it introduced.
summary: The ledger did not carry the counting_semaphore slot, the SlotRelease guard, or the MutationGate ticket as acquire/release pairs — and the ticket was precisely the omission that a ledger exists to catch, since it was the one resource still being cleaned up by hand. Written out in full as a committed fragment, including the TSan probe results for both new primitives and an explicit statement that no manual cleanup remains, so the documented-impossibility exception is not invoked anywhere in this diff.
classification_rationale: A contract artefact incomplete for the code it covers.

trigger: A Windows host with roughly 1,600 or more inbound firewall rules — ordinary on a GPO-managed enterprise host — that this plugin contained, and whose prior-policy record is missing.
summary: The `name=all` discriminator consulted `tool_ran && exit_code == 0` but not `output_truncated`. A capture that hits the runner's 1MB blob cap satisfies both — the runner drains, the child exits normally — and OUR rules are added last, so they are in the dropped tail. The probe then answers 'not ours' on a host we contained, the block/block capture is stored AS the restore image, and release replays it: policy back to block/block, allow rules deleted, device cut off from its own management channel, release reporting success. Note the direction — before this discriminator existed the belt always held and release fell back to the RECOVERABLE Microsoft default, so getting truncation wrong converted a recoverable outcome into an unrecoverable one. Truncation is now a failed read.
classification_rationale: A truncated capture was read as a complete one.

trigger: A C++ diff whose Resource Ledger omits an fd-owning boundary it introduced.
summary: The ledger carried a row for the new std::ofstream and none for the new std::ifstream in linux_ipv6_stack_present, while asserting outright that nothing in the diff acquires an fd — false the moment that function was added, and inconsistent with its own neighbouring row. Added, with the standing sentence corrected and the omission recorded rather than quietly patched.
classification_rationale: A contract artefact contradicting itself.

trigger: bad_alloc, or any other exception, from the refresher's tick body.
summary: An exception escaping a std::thread entry is std::terminate — the whole process, from a best-effort cache refresh. The tick allocates (the id set, and list_quarantined's own vector), so it is reachable. Worse, the Resource Ledger row ASSERTED the body could not throw and was wrong on both of its stated grounds. Per-tick try/catch added, matching the five other background loops in this file that already carry it, and the ledger row corrected.
classification_rationale: The ledger asserted a property the code did not have.

trigger: A future tuning of the containment-read bound.
summary: The bound appeared as a literal 4 in the member's type, in the refresher's guard and as a function-local constant, with the RAII guard type declared twice. Collapsed to one class-scope constant and one shared guard. Also: the batch audit copied the denied vector to sort it, on the dispatch thread — the allocation shape the fail-closed path had just been changed to avoid — so it now takes the vector by value and the three call sites move into it.
classification_rationale: Duplication that would drift on first tuning.

trigger: Sustained containment-read degradation.
summary: The refresher competes for the same four slots as dispatch with no reserved permit, and std::counting_semaphore is not FIFO — so under sustained degradation the snapshot can starve exactly when it is the fallback. Left as is: a slot timeout on the dispatch path already fails closed, so the failure mode the starvation would produce is the safe one, and a reserved permit would mean the refresher can pin a connection a dispatch cannot use.
classification_rationale: An accepted cost, recorded with why the obvious fix is refused.

trigger: `quarantine.status` or `unquarantine` on a Windows host whose verbose `show rule` output exceeds the runner's ~1MB capture cap — roughly 1,600+ inbound rules, ordinary under GPO.
summary: The truncation rule was established at ONE of the four sites that parse `netsh ... show rule name=all`. The other three carried the same defect with worse consequences: win_is_quarantined reported `state|inactive` on a contained host — bypassing the CDX-P1-04 `uncertain` guard via the one failure mode it cannot see — and win_unquarantine got an empty delete list, attempted nothing, left teardown_failed false and reported `status|released` rc 0 while every allow rule survived and the stored prior policy was cleared. Extracted as a pure, unit-tested `netsh_capture_usable` and applied at all four, with win_unquarantine flipping teardown_failed on an untrustworthy list and win_get_whitelist noting a possibly-partial answer. The reviewer noted the composite was not made functionally worse by the one-site fix — but a decided rule that three of its four sites contradict is how the drift this file warns about begins.
classification_rationale: A rule applied at one of four sites that share its premise.

trigger: Any non-fail-closed dispatch with at least one quarantined target via the dispatch_closure or legacy sites.
summary: `std::move` on a `const auto` object yields `const T&&`, which cannot bind to the move constructor and silently selects the COPY — so two of the three call sites still copied, while the comment claimed the move made it free. Verified by the reviewer with a minimal repro. The two declarations are now non-const so the move is real, and the comment records the trap.
classification_rationale: A comment asserting an optimisation the language did not perform.

trigger: Reading the Resource Ledger's containment-read-slot row.
summary: The one row the previous commit did not touch named `SlotRelease` — a type that no longer exists anywhere in the tree — omitted the new owner's non-copyable/no-move property that the schema asks for, and asserted there is no early return or throw in the acquire-to-release window, which the neighbouring row added in the SAME commit falsifies. Adjudicated as NOT a ledger-omission floor: no owning boundary is missing, which is what that floor covers; this is a stale row, now corrected. Recorded rather than quietly fixed because it is the round's own pattern at the artefact level — the fix that corrected one row falsified its neighbour.
classification_rationale: A ledger row naming a type that does not exist and a property the code lacks.

trigger: Any future edit to the netsh capture-usability test.
summary: The discriminator had no coverage — it sat inline in a Windows-only, subprocess-spawning shell function with no pure seam, in a file whose own convention is pure tested helpers. Closed by the same extraction as F1: `netsh_capture_usable` is pure, lives at the agent-parser level (~5x headroom per the test-efficiency discipline), spawns nothing, and has a test covering the truncation case a two-field check cannot see plus each independent failure.
classification_rationale: Missing coverage of a decision on a security-reporting path.

trigger: Compiling quarantine_plugin.cpp for any non-Windows target. No configuration or input needed.
summary: There are THREE `WhitelistRead` definitions, one per platform #ifdef, and the `note` member was added to the Windows one only — while the emit site that reads `wl.note` sits OUTSIDE the #ifdef chain. The macOS and Linux agent legs did not compile. Fixed by adding the member to all three, with a comment on each saying why it must exist there even though only Windows sets it. THE PROCESS FAILURE MATTERS MORE THAN THE DEFECT: the commit that introduced it claimed 'Verified: 284 assertions agent-side', and that verification could not have caught it — the quarantine plugin is a separate dylib target and is NOT a dependency of yuzu_agent_tests, so the test binary relinked while the plugin object stayed at its pre-change timestamp. A passing test suite was offered as evidence for a build it never performed. Every later verification in this run uses `meson compile` with no target filter.
classification_rationale: A build leg broken by this change, and a green test presented as evidence for it.

trigger: Any non-fail-closed dispatch with at least one quarantined target via the dispatch_closure or legacy sites.
summary: SUPERSEDES the `fixed` row: the fix was recorded as applied and was NOT. The replacement strings did not match the real declarations (which carry `yuzu::server::` qualifiers), so the commit changed only the comment — leaving two artefacts, the in-code comment and the ledger row, both asserting a non-const declaration that did not exist. The ledger's own `fixed` disposition was closure evidence for an open finding, which is the failure mode the records-vs-tests split exists to prevent. Now genuinely applied and confirmed by reading the two lines back, and a third site that a mis-targeted replace had changed by accident was restored.
classification_rationale: A recorded fix that was never made.

trigger: Reading either comment; any future call site added on the strength of one of them.
